I’ve just created the type chart module, which defines the effectiveness multipliers for all Gen 3 types. The next logical piece of the engine is handling player input, because the overworld, menus, and battle screens will all rely on a unified input system. 

First, I consider what the rest of the codebase expects. In the index.html I already set up a canvas with id “screen” and a hint element. The upcoming game loop (not yet written) will likely call something like `Input.held('up')` or `Input.press('a')` each frame. I need a module that:
- Maps physical keyboard keys to logical game actions (directional movement, A/B buttons, menu).
- Tracks both the held state (for continuous movement) and edge‑triggered presses (so a button press is consumed only once per frame, preventing repeated actions when the key is held).
- Provides a way to reset the per‑frame press flags at the end of each frame.
- Exposes a helper for getting the current direction (up/down/left/right) in a single call, which will simplify movement code.

I also recall that the audio system uses a function `Audio2.unlock()` to enable sound on the first user interaction, so the keydown handler should call that to satisfy browsers’ autoplay policies.

Given these requirements, I decide to create a new JavaScript file `input.js` under `js/`. The content will be a self‑executing module that attaches an `Input` object to `window`. Inside, I’ll define a `KEYMAP` object translating the relevant `KeyboardEvent.code` values to logical names:
- Arrow keys and WASD for directions.
- Z, Enter, Space for the “A” button (confirm/interact).
- X and Escape for the “B” button (cancel/run).
- M and Backquote (`) for opening the menu.

I’ll need two internal state objects: `held` (boolean per logical key) and `pressed` (edge flag). On `keydown`, I’ll look up the logical key; if it’s not already held, I’ll set `pressed[k] = true` to record the edge. Then I’ll set `held[k] = true`. I also call `e.preventDefault()` to stop the browser from scrolling, and `Audio2.unlock()` to satisfy the audio policy.

On `keyup`, I simply clear the held flag.

The returned API should include:
- `held(k)`: returns true if the key is currently down.
- `press(k)`: returns the edge flag and clears it (so it’s true only once per physical press).
- `endFrame()`: clears all `pressed` flags at the end of a frame (in case any were not consumed).
- `dirHeld()`: a convenience that returns the first active direction in priority order (up, down, left, right) or null.

All of this matches the pattern used elsewhere in the project (e.g., the audio unlock call in other modules). I’ll now write this as a single string literal for the file, preserving proper indentation and line breaks, and issue a Write tool call to create `D:\project-5\js\input.js` with the content.

This will give the engine a solid input foundation for the overworld, menus, and battle system, and fits naturally after establishing the type chart.
